question: to the Commission Katri Kulmuni (Renew) Subject:

Northern Europe’s climate and limited daylight significantly restrict the open-field production of organic crops, making the production of such crops in greenhouses an essential part of Finland’s domestic food supply. Finnish production is local, small-scale, pesticide-free and highly valued by consumers. Extending the derogation for organic greenhouse production is necessary because northern and arctic growing conditions severely limit open-field organic cultivation. Without it, domestic organic greenhouse production is likely to decline, with imports, or more likely, conventional greenhouse vegetables replacing it. This would undermine the objectives of the EU organic regulation. The current rules also support investment and production development, while Finnish organic greenhouse production serves only the domestic market and does not distort competition within the EU. With this in mind: 1.

How does the Commission assess whether removing the derogation for organic greenhouse production would promote the objectives of the EU organic regulation if it is likely to reduce domestic organic production in Finland and increase reliance on imports or conventional greenhouse production?
If the derogation is removed, how will the Commission ensure that consumers continue to have access to domestically produced organic greenhouse vegetables?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.9.2026) The derogation on growing crops in demarcated beds is only allowed for the surfaces that were certified as organic for that practice before 28 June 2017 in Finland, Sweden, Denmark, and on Norway, where it applies under the European Economic Area (EEA) agreement. The derogation expires on 31/12/20311. The Commission has commissioned a study on this issue. This study assessed the use, relevance, coherence and potential future implications of discontinuing the derogation allowing demarcated beds in certified organic greenhouse production. It will be made public in the second half of 2026 to inform subsequent discussions on this subject.
1 Point 1.5 of Part I of Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2018/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council of

30 May 2018 on organic production and labelling of organic products and repealing Council Regulation (EC) No 834/2007, OJ L 150 14.6.2018, p.1. ELI: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2018/848/2024-12-01.
